## What The Business Is

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is the largest U.S.-based diversified bank by scale, with global operations across consumer banking, corporate and investment banking, commercial banking, payments, markets, and asset/wealth management. As of March 31, 2026, the firm reported **$4.9 trillion of assets** and **$364 billion of stockholders’ equity**, serving U.S. consumers and small businesses under the Chase brand and corporate, institutional, government, and wealth clients globally under J.P. Morgan and related brands. ([jpmorganchase.com](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/content/dam/jpmc/jpmorgan-chase-and-co/investor-relations/documents/quarterly-earnings/2026/1st-quarter/a5fd2d13-877b-43b2-8b58-81bad4399c87.pdf?hss_meta=eyJvcmdhbml6YXRpb25faWQiOiAxMTUsICJncm91cF9pZCI6IDU5MjQ2LCAiYXNzZXRfaWQiOiA0NjQ0NzksICJncm91cF9jb250ZW50X2lkIjogNzMwNTU5LCAiZ3JvdXBfbmV0d29ya19jb250ZW50X2lkIjogNzUzMzkyfQ%3D%3D&utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

The business is organized around major franchises: **Consumer & Community Banking**—deposits, credit cards, auto, home lending, branches and digital banking; **Commercial & Investment Bank**—M&A/advisory, underwriting, treasury services, lending, fixed income and equities markets; **Asset & Wealth Management**—investment management, private banking, brokerage and retirement-related assets; and **Corporate**—treasury, capital, liquidity and other firm-level items. In the Q1 2026 call excerpt, management said CCB generated **$5.0 billion** of net income, CIB **$9.0 billion**, and AWM **$1.8 billion**, underscoring the firm’s broad earnings mix across retail banking, markets/investment banking, and fee-based wealth/asset management.

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Q1 2026 was strong: JPMorgan reported **$16.5 billion of net income**, **$5.94 EPS**, **23% ROTCE**, and **$50.5 billion of revenue**, helped by higher Markets revenue, Asset Management and Investment Banking fees, and net interest income. The transcript also noted IB fees up **28% year over year**, fixed income markets up **21%**, equities up **17%**, AUM of **$4.8 trillion** up **16%**, and client assets of **$7.1 trillion** up **18%**.

Capital return capacity remains a positive signal. After the 2026 Fed stress-test process, JPMorgan announced plans to raise its quarterly common dividend to **$1.65 from $1.50** for Q3 2026 and authorized a new **$50 billion** common share repurchase program effective July 1, 2026; it also said its current SCB remains **2.5%** through September 30, 2027 and its standardized CET1 requirement including buffers remains **11.5%**. ([jpmorganchase.com](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/ir/news/2026/jpmc-dividend-increase-common-share-repurchase?utm_source=openai))

The broader banking-system read-through was also constructive: all **32** large banks passed the Fed’s 2026 stress test, with the Fed’s severely adverse scenario including a rise in unemployment to **10%**, a **4.6%** GDP contraction, a **30%** housing-price decline, and a **58%** stock-market drop. JPMorgan followed the results with its dividend/buyback announcement. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/dbb5f33becf7240fbb9a85fa2befd8f3?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

Management continues to flag capital-rule pressure. In the Q1 transcript, CFO Jeremy Barnum said the Basel III endgame and G-SIB reproposals could raise JPMorgan’s CET1 capital need by about **4%** under the proposed rules, with the firm needing to plan for a **5.2% G-SIB surcharge in 2028**, up from **4.5%**, implying about **$20 billion** of additional G-SIB-related capital on the current balance sheet. Management argued this could raise the cost of credit and discourage some markets activity.

Credit and macro risks are not benign. Q1 credit costs were **$2.5 billion**, including **$2.3 billion** of net charge-offs and a **$191 million** reserve build, while management kept the 2026 Card net charge-off outlook at about **3.4%**. Jamie Dimon also warned in the call that a future credit cycle could produce losses “worse than people expect,” even if he did not view private credit as systemic based on its relative size.

Expenses are rising alongside business growth and compensation. The transcript showed Q1 expenses of **$26.9 billion**, up **14% year over year**, driven by compensation, front-office headcount growth, brokerage expense, distribution fees, and the absence of a prior-year FDIC special accrual release; full-year adjusted expense guidance remained about **$105 billion**.

Recent operational and leadership items add monitoring points. JPMorgan promoted Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh to co-presidents, while longtime executive Marianne Lake is set to retire at year-end, changing the CEO-succession field. ([washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/06/25/jpmorgan-dimon-retirement-doug-petno-troy-rohrbaugh/e729dcbe-70ae-11f1-8730-e7fd0e2a6404_story.html?utm_source=openai)) Separately, reported WARN/layoff notices included **244** planned job cuts in Plano, Texas tied to an August 2026 call-center shutdown, plus smaller California cuts, suggesting ongoing efficiency and location reshaping despite strong firmwide profitability. ([layofftracker.us](https://www.layofftracker.us/layoffs/company/jpmorgan-chase/2026?utm_source=openai))

- Q1 2026 net income of $16.5B ($66B annualized run-rate) with 23% ROTCE shows earnings power above the $57.5B TTM level.
- Fee momentum is broad: IB fees +28% y/y, FICC +21%, equities +17%, AUM +16% to $4.8T — diversified growth beyond NII.
- Capital return is aggressive: dividend raised to $1.65/quarter and a new $50B buyback (≈5.5% of market cap) shrinks share count and supports per-share value; SCB held at 2.5%.
- If markets/IB strength persists, forward NI could reach $63–66B; at 16x, market cap approaches $1.0–1.05T.

## Bear Case
- Basel III endgame / G-SIB reproposal could require ~4% more CET1 (~$20B), constraining returns and some markets activity.
- Credit is normalizing: $2.5B Q1 credit costs, Card NCOs guided ~3.4%, and Dimon warning the next credit cycle could be "worse than people expect."
- Expenses rose 14% y/y in Q1 ($26.9B), with ~$105B full-year guide compressing operating leverage.
- The stock already trades near 15.8x TTM earnings — rich versus its own history (3-yr avg NI/MC of 8.2% implies ~12.2x); multiple compression to 13–14x on $58–60B NI gives ~$780–830B.

## Logic
- **Forward net income:** TTM NI is $57.5B; Q1 2026 annualizes to ~$66B, but markets revenue is likely above trend and credit costs should drift higher. I blend to a forward NI of **~$61,000M** (+6% vs TTM), consistent with fee growth, stable NII, and modest reserve builds.
- **Applied multiple:** Current implied P/E is ~15.8x (NI/MC of 6.3%). Given premium ROTCE (23%), best-in-class franchise, and heavy buybacks, JPM warrants a premium to the 3-yr average (~12.2x), but capital-rule and credit headwinds argue against expansion. I apply **15.5x**.
- **Forward market cap:** 61,000 × 15.5 ≈ **$945,500M**, roughly +4% from the current $908.9B — earnings growth partly offset by slight multiple normalization.
- FCF is not meaningful for a bank (TTM FCF −$107.7B reflects balance-sheet flows), so it is excluded from valuation.
